why: I checked every command in both briefs. Most of them are fine: `npm test` maps to the `node --test` script, and the Check 1, Check 2 and Check 4 one-liners have valid syntax. Check 3 is the problem. It wraps the JavaScript in a double-quoted shell string and writes `new RegExp('\\b'+f+'\\b')`. Inside bash double quotes, `\\` turns into a single `\`, so Node receives `'\b'`. In a JS string that is a backspace character, not a regex word boundary. The pattern then never matches any README heading, so the check would print every export as "missing" even when the README is correct. The command runs, but not as intended: the shell escaping breaks the JavaScript it delivers, so a correct PR would fail. The criterion therefore fails for the verifier brief.
